title: Bloch's theorem (complex analysis)
intro: In complex analysis, a branch of mathematics, Bloch's theorem describes the behaviour of holomorphic functions defined on the unit disk. It gives a lower bound on the size of a disk in which an inverse to a holomorphic function exists.

title: Block-stacking problem
intro: In statics, the block-stacking problem (sometimes known as The Leaning Tower of Lire (Johnson 1955), also the book-stacking problem, harmonic staircase, or a number of other similar terms) is a puzzle concerning the stacking of blocks at the edge of a table.

title: Block walking
intro: In combinatorial mathematics, block walking is a method useful in thinking about sums of combinations graphically as "walks" on Pascal's triangle. As the name suggests, block walking problems involve counting the number of ways an individual can walk from one corner A of a city block to another corner B of another city block given restrictions on the number of blocks the person may walk, the directions the person may travel, the distance from A to B, et cetera.

title: Blockchain privacy
intro: Blockchain privacy describes how blockchain systems handle the confidentiality of transaction and record data. Many public blockchains can provide pseudonymity, while ledger transparency can allow transaction tracing through analysis of on-chain activity and related information.

title: Blow-up lemma
intro: The blow-up lemma, proved by János Komlós, Gábor N. Sárközy, and Endre Szemerédi in 1997, is an important result in extremal graph theory, particularly within the context of the regularity method. It states that the regular pairs in the statement of Szemerédi's regularity lemma behave like complete bipartite graphs in the context of embedding spanning graphs of bounded degree.

title: Blue Planet Software
categories: United States video game company stubs
intro: Blue Planet Software Inc. was an American video game developer and publisher founded by Henk Rogers in Honolulu, Hawaii in 1995.

title: Bluetooth Low Energy denial of service attacks
resolved_title: Bluetooth Low Energy denial of service attacks
intro: The Bluetooth Low Energy denial of service attacks are a series of denial-of-service attacks against mobile phones and iPads via Bluetooth Low Energy that can make it difficult to use them.

title: Blum–Goldwasser cryptosystem
intro: The Blum–Goldwasser (BG) cryptosystem is an asymmetric key encryption algorithm proposed by Manuel Blum and Shafi Goldwasser in 1984.  Blum–Goldwasser is a probabilistic, semantically secure cryptosystem with a constant-size ciphertext expansion.

It is centered on the Belcher family – parents Bob and Linda and their three children, Tina, Gene, and Louise – who run a burger restaurant in New Jersey and often go on adventures of many kinds.
